purpose: one baseline through the runner's existing training and validation contract, on the accepted pins-planning-appeal-outcome artifact, plus the derived paired model-vs-reference intervals

artifact.name: pins-planning-appeal-outcome
artifact.split_description: temporal split on the VALIDATION instant, the shipped time column: train = appeals validated before 2020-01-01, eval = validated 2020-01-01..2021-12-31, holdout = validated on or after 2022-01-01. The candidate record's provisional partition was by decision year; the outcome date cannot ship (it is post-instant information) and the qualification gate requires disjoint split ranges on a shipped time column, so the split key moved to the instant - the same construction as the published ipo-trademark-registration-outcome (filed_date) and ec-merger-phase2-opening (notification_date) tasks. Slow cases mean a split's labels can postdate the next split's earliest instants; label timing is declared unverified and the artifact is retrospective research only.

model_vs_references.purpose: derived evidence, not the runner: paired model-vs-reference intervals on identical eval rows after the verbatim contract run
model_vs_references.model: XGBClassifier n_estimators=30 max_depth=6 lr=0.1 hist seed 42 - identical to the verbatim train.py baseline; string columns with >1000 levels dropped exactly as the baseline drops them
model_vs_references.scope: eval rows only (28104 rows, validation instants 2020-2021); the holdout was never opened
notes: the references are reimplemented here independently (pandas groupby), not imported from the build job's score.py
shipped_rate_feature scores the artifact's own lpa_allow_rate_prior column; its agreement with lpa_hist_rate cross-checks the reference
intervals containing zero are inconclusive differences, not parity

scope: runner-contract baseline plus derived reference intervals; no agent loop, no holdout evaluation. Holdout stays sealed until the design is frozen.
